title: Nicholls and Phillips Rescue New Zealand After Bumrah's Early Burst in Wellington
excerpt: From 70 for 5, an unbroken 173-run stand carried New Zealand to 243 for 5 on day one of the first Test at the Basin Reserve.
body:
• New Zealand recovered from 70 for 5 to close day one of the first Test in Wellington on 243 for 5 in 82 overs.
  • Henry Nicholls (113 not out) and Glenn Phillips (94 not out) added an unbroken 173 for the sixth wicket; Nicholls' hundred was his 12th in Tests and his fifth at the Basin Reserve.
  • Jasprit Bumrah took 3 for 52 and Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep one wicket each after Shubman Gill chose to bowl on a green surface.
  • Day two starts with Phillips six runs short of a century and India needing early wickets with the second new ball; the match runs to November 23 and is on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV in India.

India had the day they asked for by lunch, and a very different one by stumps. Having chosen to bowl on a Basin Reserve surface carrying 15mm of grass, Shubman Gill's attack reduced New Zealand to 70 for 5 early in the second session — then did not take another wicket. Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips batted through the rest of the day in an unbroken 173-run stand that carried the hosts to 243 for 5 at the close of the first Test's opening day.

Bumrah sets the morning up

The start was ominous for New Zealand. Tom Latham shouldered arms to Jasprit Bumrah in the first over and lost his off stump. Anshul Kamboj, sharing the new ball, had Devon Conway caught behind in his second over, shortly after Conway had overturned a caught-behind decision off Bumrah. Nicholls, batting at No. 3 in Kane Williamson's place, added 39 with Rachin Ravindra, who survived a missed review and a run-out chance before Akash Deep had him edging behind. Bumrah then removed Daryl Mitchell, pinned by an inside edge onto his thigh pad, and New Zealand went to lunch at 60 for 4. Tom Blundell fell to Bumrah soon after the break — a hard-length ball that seamed away and took the edge to Gill at first slip — and at 70 for 5 the decision to bowl first looked fully vindicated. Bumrah finished the day with 3 for 52.

The stand that took the day away

The partnership began with a reprieve: India reviewed a Bumrah nip-backer against Phillips believing it had struck pad, but the TV umpire stayed with the on-field call. From there the pair's control tightened measurably — New Zealand's false-shot percentage fell from 25.1 in the morning session to 13.6 in the second, according to Cricbuzz, and the hosts lost no wicket in either session after Blundell's.

Phillips passed 1,000 Test runs in the first over after tea and reached his fifty with a back cut off a fresh Bumrah spell. Nicholls brought up his hundred — his 12th in Tests, and his fifth at this ground in 15 innings, ESPNcricinfo reported — and then survived the day's most damning moment for India: on 102 he top-edged a pull off Prasidh Krishna to Devdutt Padikkal at backward square leg, only for Rishabh Pant to charge into the fielder's eyeline and the catch to go down. India took the second new ball as soon as it was due but bowled only 82 overs despite a half-hour extension. The full scorecard is on ESPNcricinfo.

The selection question

India's four-man pace attack left out Mohammed Siraj, and Ravindra Jadeja made way for Washington Sundar against New Zealand's left-hand-heavy line-up. As the stand grew and the older ball offered Kamboj and Akash Deep little, Cricbuzz noted India missing the long, miserly spells Siraj bowls. Former India wicketkeeper Dinesh Karthik, speaking on Cricbuzz, set the target for day two: "Anything under 320, India will be very happy... For me, India has to try and stop New Zealand by 320-325. If not, it is going to be very tough."

"India has to try and stop New Zealand by 320-325. If not, it is going to be very tough."

— Dinesh Karthik, on Cricbuzz

What happens next

Day two resumes on Friday, November 20, with Nicholls on 113 and Phillips six short of a hundred. The first hour decides the shape of the match: break the stand early and India's morning work still counts; let it run and a side that was 70 for 5 will post the kind of total that bats India out of the game on a pitch expected to ease further. The two-Test series counts toward the 2025-27 World Test Championship cycle.

Brief scores: New Zealand 243/5 in 82 overs (Henry Nicholls 113*, Glenn Phillips 94*; Jasprit Bumrah 3-52, Akash Deep 1-33, Anshul Kamboj 1-57) vs India.
